readback.name: flatCovariantDerivative_contMDiff
readback.mathematical_statement: For independent universes u_1,u_2, an implicit nontrivially normed field K : Type u_1, an implicit normed additive group E : Type u_2 with NormedSpace K E, and arbitrary implicit order k : WithTop ENat, the flatCovariantDerivative K E satisfies CovariantDerivative.ContMDiffCovariantDerivative at order k. This is the manifold-regularity predicate for that connection on E with the self model, not regularity of arbitrary vector fields. No completeness or finite-dimensionality assumptions occur, and K is not restricted to R. The order k is arbitrary, rather than a particular printed infinity value. No curvature, torsion, metric or global-manifold existence result is asserted by this interface.

readback.name: mdiffAt_vectorSpace_iff_differentiableAt
readback.mathematical_statement: For independent universes u_1,u_2, an implicit nontrivially normed field K : Type u_1 and normed K-vector space E : Type u_2, implicit tangent section sigma : (x : E) -> TangentSpace I(K,E) x and implicit x : E, manifold differentiability at x of the total-space section y |-> Bundle.TotalSpace.mk' E y (sigma(y)), from self model I(K,E) to its product with itself, is equivalent to ordinary K-Frechet differentiability of sigma at x. The tangent-family base and bundle codomain are explicitly E. On this vector-space manifold the tangent fibers identify with E. This is an equivalence, with no differentiability assumed in advance, and no completeness, finite-dimensionality, metric or nonflat-manifold hypothesis.

readback.name: flatCovariantDerivative
readback.mathematical_statement: For explicit nontrivially normed field K : Type u_1 and explicit normed K-vector space E : Type u_2, with their normed-field, normed-group and normed-space instances implicit, flatCovariantDerivative K E is CovariantDerivative data on the self-model manifold E and its tangent family x |-> TangentSpace I(K,E) x. The supplied definition applies to a section sigma at x by fderiv K sigma x. No completeness, finite-dimensionality or inner product is required. This is the standard flat connection on a vector-space model, not construction of a Levi-Civita connection or curvature data for an arbitrary manifold.

readback.name: flatCovariantDerivative_apply
readback.mathematical_statement: For independent universes u_1,u_2, an implicit nontrivially normed field K and normed K-vector space E, every explicit tangent section sigma and explicit point x satisfy (flatCovariantDerivative K E)(sigma)(x) = fderiv K sigma x. There is no differentiability hypothesis: the equality uses the library's total fderiv definition, so it must not be read as asserting that sigma is differentiable. No completeness, finite-dimensionality, metric or global regularity assumptions occur.

readback.name: mlieBracket_vectorSpace_eq
readback.mathematical_statement: For independent universes u_1,u_2, an implicit nontrivially normed field K and normed K-vector space E, every explicit tangent vector fields V,W on the self-model manifold E have manifold Lie bracket mlieBracket I(K,E) V W equal to the ordinary vector-space Lie bracket lieBracket K V W as whole fields. No differentiability assumptions are present in this identity of the defined bracket functions; it does not assert smoothness or differentiability of V,W. Completeness, finite-dimensionality and metric hypotheses are absent.

readback.name: flatCovariantDerivative_curvatureOp_eq_zero
readback.mathematical_statement: For independent universes u_1,u_2, an implicit nontrivially normed field K and normed K-vector space E, implicit tangent fields V,W,Z and implicit x : E, assume V and W are K-differentiable at x, the map fderiv K Z is K-differentiable at x, and IsSymmSndFDerivAt K Z x. Under exactly these pointwise regularity and second-Frechet-derivative symmetry premises, curvatureOp(flatCovariantDerivative K E)(V,W,Z)(x)=0 in the tangent fiber at x. No global C2 hypothesis, completeness or finite-dimensionality is stated. There is no separate DifferentiableAt K Z x premise in the displayed type. This is zero curvature for the standard flat connection under its stated test-field premises, not flatness of an arbitrary metric manifold.

readback.name: flatCovariantDerivative_torsion_eq_zero
readback.mathematical_statement: For independent universes u_1,u_2, an implicit nontrivially normed field K and normed K-vector space E, additionally assume CompleteSpace K, CompleteSpace E and FiniteDimensional K E. Then the entire torsion section of flatCovariantDerivative K E equals the zero section of continuous K-bilinear tangent-valued maps, at all base points x : E. The completeness and finite-dimensionality hypotheses are explicit and retained even if another formulation might avoid them. No real-scalar restriction or inner product is imposed. This states torsion-freeness of the model connection, not an arbitrary connection or manifold.

readback.name: flatCovariantDerivative_inner_compatible
readback.mathematical_statement: For an implicit real inner-product space F : Type u_3 with NormedAddCommGroup F and InnerProductSpace R F instances, implicit Y,Z : F -> F and implicit x : F, assume Y and Z are real-Frechet differentiable at x. For every explicit direction v : F, fderiv R (y |-> inner R (Y(y)) (Z(y))) x applied to v equals inner R (Z(x)) ((flatCovariantDerivative R F Y x)(v)) plus inner R (Y(x)) ((flatCovariantDerivative R F Z x)(v)). The order of the arguments in the first inner product is as displayed. No completeness or finite-dimensionality is required. This is compatibility with the fixed vector-space inner product and the flat connection, not compatibility with a variable metric on a general manifold. The sole declaration universe is u_3.

This is reflexive equality of the definition, not a new connection property or equality to a different construction.
